source.name: Traditional Krishna/Vrindavan story
source.episode_or_reference: Story idea supplied in stories/story_ideas.md; traditional account/folklore treatment, not presented as a direct scripture quotation.

characters.description: Warm Indian grandfather in his late 60s, white kurta-pajama, simple shawl, expressive kind face.
Indian boy aged about 10 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.
Indian girl aged about 8 in simple Indian clothes, curious expressive face.
Mother Yashoda in traditional Vrindavan sari and jewelry, warm expressive face.

Baby Krishna, approximately 6–8 years old, small child proportions and clearly pre-adolescent, blue skin, soft round childlike face, large expressive eyes, short dark curly hair, peacock-feather crown, yellow pitambar, simple traditional jewelry; never depicted as an adult or muscular teenager.

locations.description: Peaceful Vrindavan village courtyard beneath a huge old banyan tree, exposed roots, soft afternoon light, earthen ground, clay pots, village greenery and a calm storytelling atmosphere.
Gokul courtyard with a butter pot hanging unusually high from a wooden beam beneath a roof.

supporting_assets.description: Clay butter pot hanging high above reach from a sturdy wooden beam.
Distinct group of young Gokul cowherd boys in traditional simple clothing, varied faces and proportions.
Small group of playful Vrindavan monkeys gathered near a window.
